name: Accredited Cognitive Misconceptions Catalog (Pakistan NCP & Cognitive Science)
description: Formally accredited student procedural bugs and misconceptions grounded in peer-reviewed cognitive science (Brown & Burton 1978; Siegler et al. 2013; Kintsch 1978).

bugs.subject: Mathematics
bugs.name: Independent Whole-Number Addition (Whole Number Bias)
bugs.primaryCitation: Siegler, R. S., et al. (2013). Fractions: The new frontier for theories of numerical development. Trends in Cognitive Sciences, 17(1), 13-19.
bugs.description: Student treats numerator and denominator as two independent whole numbers, adding top and bottom directly.

bugs.subject: Mathematics
bugs.name: Unscaled Numerator with Common Denominator Slip
bugs.primaryCitation: Brown, J. S., & Burton, R. R. (1978). Diagnostic models for procedural bugs in basic mathematical skills. Cognitive Science, 2(2), 155-192.
bugs.description: Student identifies the common denominator k*b but adds numerators directly without scaling the first numerator by k.

bugs.subject: Mathematics
bugs.name: Inverse Magnitude Inversion (Whole Number Bias)
bugs.primaryCitation: Resnick, L. B., et al. (1989). Thinking in arithmetic and algebra. Handbook of Research on Mathematics Teaching and Learning.
bugs.description: Student concludes that 1/5 is larger than 1/4 because the whole number 5 is larger than 4.

bugs.subject: Mathematics
bugs.name: Unilateral Scaling (Numerator Only)
bugs.primaryCitation: Siegler, R. S., & Pyke, A. A. (2013). Developmental and individual differences in understanding of fractions. Developmental Psychology, 49(10), 1994.
bugs.description: When generating an equivalent fraction, student multiplies the numerator by k but leaves the denominator unchanged.

bugs.subject: Mathematics
bugs.name: Premature Simplification Termination
bugs.primaryCitation: Brown, J. S., & Burton, R. R. (1978). Diagnostic models for procedural bugs in basic mathematical skills. Cognitive Science, 2(2), 155-192.
bugs.description: Student divides numerator and denominator by 2 once and stops, failing to reduce to the lowest term.

bugs.subject: Mathematics
bugs.name: Improper-to-Mixed Number Inversion
bugs.primaryCitation: Siegler, R. S., et al. (2013). Fractions: The new frontier for theories of numerical development. Trends in Cognitive Sciences, 17(1), 13-19.
bugs.description: Student computes quotient and remainder correctly but swaps their positions in the mixed fraction.

bugs.subject: English
bugs.name: Salient Supporting Detail as Main Idea
bugs.primaryCitation: Afflerbach, P. (1990). The influence of prior knowledge on expert readers' main idea construction strategies. Reading Research Quarterly, 25(1), 31-46.
bugs.description: Student selects a specific, vivid supporting detail from the text and misidentifies it as the central main idea.

bugs.subject: English
bugs.name: Single Topic-Word Substitution
bugs.primaryCitation: Kintsch, W., & van Dijk, T. A. (1978). Toward a model of text comprehension and production. Psychological Review, 85(5), 363-394.
bugs.description: Student selects an isolated topic noun (e.g. 'Water') instead of the predicate sentence expressing what happens to it.

bugs.subject: English
bugs.name: Chronological/Causal Direction Inversion
bugs.primaryCitation: Trabasso, T., & van den Broek, P. (1985). Causal thinking and the representation of narrative events. Journal of Memory and Language, 24(5), 612-630.
bugs.description: Student confuses the cause with the effect, treating the consequence as the trigger.
